The phase-0–2 review found three recurring build-hygiene failures (now register patterns
P27/P28/P29). They are binding on every remaining task: a task may not close while
re-creating one. **P28 (strangle) is load-bearing** — without it the universal loop
becomes "one more layer over the static DAG" instead of its replacement, which is the
whole point of the slice.

**A. Concrete debts to clear while fixing phases 0–2** (each move is owner-first +
strangle, not a new parallel file):

| Debt found in the partial build | Pattern | Correct move |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Slice0SearchLedger` (`gy_loop.py`) beside canonical `SearchLedger` (`pdc/_impl/layer2_design_search.py`) | P27 | DONE first pass: `Slice0SearchLedger` extends canonical `SearchLedger`; remaining cleanup is to narrow GY sidecar fields as consumers migrate. |
| Second `AcquisitionPlanner` (`gy_loop.py`) beside `acquisition_planner.py` / `layer2_substrate_acquisition.py` | P27 | DONE first pass: GY-E delegates routing/disposition to `plan_requirement_gap_acquisition`; remaining cleanup is to move the thin façade out of `gy_loop.py`. |
| Lex-bounds rule duplicated in `gy_spine_repair.py` and `policy_design/search.py` | P27 | DONE first pass: one owner = the engine (`search.py`); GY façade calls it. |
| Two fixture catalog graphs (`_InMemorySlice0CatalogGraph` + `build_slice0_fixture_catalog_graph`) | P27 | DONE: one fixture builder over the real `DatasetCatalogGraph`; tests use the canonical builder. |
| `require_explicit_parameter_bounds=False` default still launders `None→0.0` | P28 | DONE first pass: default is explicit-bounds fail-closed; remaining legacy inferred-bounds calls must stay explicit until deleted. |
| 2674-line `gy_loop.py` holding B/D1/D2/D3/E/H | P27 (dual) | Move each gate/producer to its owning module; `gy_loop.py` keeps only the loop. |
| `ProductionLoopRunProof` hand-authored, shape-only validator | P29 | DONE: emitted from durable worker path and validator recomputes from CAS/index refs. |
| F4/F7 "closed" on a 2-record catalog corpus | P29 | Measure recall/precision on a representative corpus, or mark `surface_out_of_scope` with rationale. |

**B. Strangle protocol (P28).** A replace/subordinate task is not done until, **in the
same change**, it (1) deletes or fences the predecessor, (2) flips the default to the
corrected path, and (3) adds a guard (lint/test) that fails if a new caller reaches the
predecessor. It then persists a `StrangleReceipt` (§3.5.4) with a recomputing validator.
Legacy that genuinely cannot be cut yet is fenced as `legacy_shadow` / candidate-only
**and** listed in `remaining_callers` with a dated cut ticket — never left as a silent
default. This is exactly how GY-B2 already treats `/runs`, `/runs/nl`, and the
`workflow_run` job path; every later subordination (GY-C1 legacy nodes, GY-C2 lex/
governance, GY-F1 worker surfaces) follows the same pattern, not an additive layer.

**C. Owner-first protocol (P27).** Before `class Foo` or a new `gy_*.py`, consult the
§3.5.2 ownership map and run `grep -rl "<concept-root>" src/polisyos/{pdc/_impl,runtime/quality}`
for a live owner. If one exists, extend it. New files are for genuinely-new orchestration
contracts only. Free-growth still holds (§3.5.3): a correctly added engine asset becomes an
Operation with zero new code — if you are writing a hand-maintained list or a parallel
gate, stop.

**D. Emit-proof protocol (P29).** See the §3.5.4 P29 note: identifiers come from the run
(no placeholders), times are real, validators recompute, and any search/recall/precision
closure is measured on a representative substrate — not a fixture small enough to make the
metric vacuous. A committed Slice-0 `Slice0FixtureManifest` is allowed (§3.5.1); a
2-record corpus standing in for the *benchmark substrate* of an F4/F7 closure is not.

**E. Name-by-function protocol (P30) — so reuse is self-evident.** New files are named for
the capability they own (`workspace_loop.py`, not `gy_loop.py`); the owner-first grep (C)
is by *function word*, so it only finds owners if files are function-named. The phase-0–2
`gy_*` files are a standing P30 debt: either rename each to its function, or — where it
holds genuinely-new orchestration — add a module docstring that names the canonical owners
it extends (`SearchLedger`, `acquisition_planner`, `adapter_contracts`, `semantic_binding`,
`data_forge_binding`) and links related modules, so the next implementer reads them before
writing a parallel file. No new GY file may take a bare plan-provenance name without that
breadcrumb. Naming is not cosmetic: it decides which file the next person opens first, and
is the cheapest defense against re-creating P27.

**F. Standing gate for phases 2→5.** Every task's `Done when` now also requires: no second
live owner for any concept it touches (P27); a `StrangleReceipt` for any path it replaces,
with the default flipped (P28); function-named modules with owner breadcrumbs, never a bare
plan name (P30); and run-emitted, recomputed proof packets on a representative substrate
(P29). Checked at design review and at closeout, alongside the matrix/GX gates. A task whose
local tests pass but that leaves a parallel owner, an un-strangled default, a plan-named
file with no owner breadcrumb, or an authorial proof is **not done**.

### 3.5.6 Substrate / binding lift completeness gates (the GY-S lesson — binding for every lift / resolution / binding task)

The GY-S substrate lifts (S1 data-state, S2 knowledge, S3 intervention) cost many adversarial
rounds because each shipped a **shell** that passed its own narrow probes: coverage looked green but
on a curated subset; authority was **supplied, not derived**; the contract exercised only the
happy-path. The failure **escaped one level deeper each round** — for S3 the supplied authority went
caller-supplied → hardcoded code-table → hand-injected into git-ignored data → relocated into a
tracked JSON the runtime merely *trusted*; for S2 it was percent-only units / single-row lineage /
weight-synthetic contested. The disposition is always the same: **derive through the real owner +
validate (fail-closed on a fake input), never supply; be generic over the data, not enumerated; and
make the gate exercise the decisive property.** Four gates are now **binding on every task that
lifts, resolves, or binds authority** (the GY-S block and the cycle tasks N2/N4/N7/N8/N9 — their
contracts must encode all four for their decisive property):

1. **Full-denominator coverage.** Measure coverage against the **full real vocabulary** (count the
   real source files / registries), never a curated subset or a 2-record corpus. A green `N/N` is
   load-bearing only when `N` is the full real denominator — prove the denominator (`P10`).
2. **Fail-closed on a fake / novel input.** A binding to a **non-existent owner target** (a slot not
   in the real world model / `GlobalState`, a provision not in real L3), an unknown unit, or an
   out-of-domain parameter **must fail closed**. This proves the runtime **validates through the
   real owner**, not merely trusts a declared / curated / supplied value (`P32`, the
   resolve→content-bind→validate root). A tracked binding artifact is legitimate **only** if it is
   owner-validated this way — a JSON the runtime trusts is just a relocated name-map.
3. **Data-only free-grow.** A genuinely **new** entry (knob / law / family / claim / threshold)
   added via **data alone** must lift with **zero code change**; a malformed one fails closed. This
   proves the mechanism is **generic over the data**, not an enumerated / name-substring branch
   (Rule 12, `P31`). Reusing an existing mechanism for the "novel" case is a fake free-grow.
4. **The contract mutates the DECISIVE validation property (`P29`).** The behavioral contract must
   include a remove-the-property mutation for the **decisive** property — the fail-closed-on-fake
   owner validation of gate 2 — not only coverage / free-grow / no-hardcode. The gate must go **red**
   if owner-validation is removed while the happy-path bindings stay valid. A runtime that is correct
   today but whose contract would not catch that regression is **not done** (this is the exact
   verifier-completeness gap that held S3 to its last round).

Every impl/audit prompt and every `Done when` for a lift/resolution/binding task front-loads these
four — so the implementer builds to them on the first pass instead of rediscovering them through
rounds. Verification stays **targeted** (§Commands; blast-radius + recomputing validators + ruff +
guardrails), never full pytest.
```

### 3.5.4 Required proof packets (anti-P01/P05/P08/P10/P25)

The following packets are not optional prose reports. Each named high-risk task must
persist the packet as a generated artifact with a recomputing validator. The packet is
the acceptance surface: reviewers should inspect fields, not only task summaries.

- **`ProductionLoopRunProof`** (GY-B2/GY-L/GY-V2): `{run_id, job_id, endpoint,
  job_kind, enqueued_at, worker_lease_id, worker_id, _execute_workflow_invocation_id,
  workspace_loop_invocation_id, control_store_state_transitions, input_artifacts,
  output_search_exit_contract_ref, output_cas_refs, artifacts_index_refs,
  surface_reads_checked, legacy_path_disposition}`. Required path:
  `enqueue_job -> ControlWorker -> _execute_workflow -> WorkspaceLoop -> CAS +
  artifacts_index + /runs readback`. A direct helper call does not satisfy this proof.
- **`Slice0FixtureManifest`** (GY-B/GY-D1/GY-H): `{fixture_id,
  construct_scope_query, jurisdiction, population, time_horizon,
  expected_catalog_binding_refs, expected_connector_profile,
  expected_producer_root_kind, expected_terminal, forbidden_terminals,
  negative_controls}`. The manifest is the committed source of truth for Slice-0
  fixture expectations; implementation may not replace it with an inline fixture table
  or a prose "World-Bank style" label.
- **`AuthorityDerivationTrace`** (GY-A2/GY-B/GY-V4): `{operation_invocation_id,
  output_artifact_ref, declared_authority_transform, computed_evidence_kind,
  computed_decision_grade, producer_root_classes, method_classification,
  applicability_result_ref, calibration_refs, counterexamples_closed,
  certified_envelope_ref, unresolved_blockers, resulting_authority_boundary_ref,
  transform_mismatch_disposition}`. This is the audit trail for `A.verify`; an
  Operation-declared transform is an input hint only and cannot be the stamped result.
- **`AuthorityCandidateInventory`** (GY-F3/GY-V4): one row per candidate-positive
  status, including `{producer_component, source_artifact_ref, field_path, status_text,
  candidate_positive_rule, firewall_name, exclusion_reason, resulting_boundary_ref,
  false_exclusion_review, reviewer, reviewed_at}`. The count must reconcile to 406 on
  the Task-0 baseline, and false exclusions must become explicit repair tickets.
- **`CASIntegrityReport`** (GY-F2/GY-V5): `{artifact_ref, payload_digest,

  duplicate_group_id, referrers, report_index_refs, lineage_refs, tamper_probe_result,

- **`TimeSourceEnvelopeAudit`** (GY-F3/GY-V5): `{catalog_watermark,

## GY-M1 — `not_executed`

**Deciding result:** GY lifecycle audit is not green; its own real audit artifact is unregistered.

**Task's exact plan text, read before implementation:** `policy-engine/docs/plans/active/layer3-slices/GY-engine-subordination.md`, lines 1924–1933.

> - **GY-M1 — Artifact-family lifecycle registration (PHASE-0 HARD GATE).**
>   build-new/extend-existing. Finding: F18. **Must land before any GY task emits a new
>   committed artifact** — otherwise the build (and even the V-battery) produces unregistered
>   surfaces, recreating the exact gap Task 0 found. Register the GY/loop generated/
>   public-surface family in `architecture/generated_artifacts.toml` + `inventory.json`
>   with owner / regeneration command / stale-output behavior / drift gate; decide the
>   classification (`generated_committed` / `source_committed` / `surface_out_of_scope`).
>   Done when: a new GY artifact cannot be committed without a registered lifecycle entry
>   (a drift gate enforces it), and the generated-public-lifecycle validator is green for
>   the GY family.

A failing historical selected predicate may reproduce, pass, or be unmeasurable here; no current verdict is predicted from the standing label. The lane's more specific prediction, when recorded, follows.

**Prediction.** I expected an existing gate whose scoped check might miss a new unregistered
artifact. **That suspicion was not reproduced by the tested removal/new-file probes.** Both
properties were detected. The other explicit conjunct is false: the current GY-family audit
is not green, and the lifecycle-audit artifact itself lacks a generated-artifact output claim.

**Station.** The standard CLI refused the shared-root interpreter. Importing the actual
registry validator's producer modules also enforces an isolation-local interpreter and OR-Tools
backend. Those are station limitations, not product findings. I created a disposable tracked-file
copy under `_build/gy-census/root/snapshot/policy-engine`, excluding the prohibited register and
ledger without opening them. Git's index and tree independently reconcile the complete selected
file set; readback compared all 10,601 copied file paths byte-for-byte with the unchanged target,
with no mismatch or unreadable file. The source universe before exclusions was 10,603 tracked
files, all file types, under `policy-engine/`. The copy is not an auxiliary Git worktree.

An offline scratch-local venv uses Python 3.14.0 and reads existing dependency site-packages
through a `.pth`; the required OR-Tools wheel was unavailable offline, so the dependency was
installed only into that disposable venv. Local installed versions: ortools 9.15.6755, numpy
2.5.3, pandas 3.0.5, protobuf 6.33.6, absl-py 2.5.0, immutabledict 4.3.1,
python-dateutil 2.9.0.post0, six 1.17.0, typing-extensions 4.16.0. No package/configuration in
the measured worktree was changed. This is explicitly a dependency-equipped scratch station,
not a claim that the original CLI station was healthy.

**Measurement.** The unchanged production functions
`validate_gy_lifecycle_registry(snapshot)` and `validate(audit, repo_root=snapshot)` run to
completion. The registry returns `fail`. Deciding example, independently reconciled against
the complete parsed TOML family/output set:

```json
{"code":"layer3_gy_artifact_not_registered","path":"architecture/policy_design_case/layer3_gy_task0_audit/layer3_gy_generated_public_lifecycle_audit.json"}
```

That artifact has no family claiming it in `architecture/generated_artifacts.toml`.
Further current GY producer wrappers lack callable `declared_outputs`: the N10 CG1/L2 census,
N13a acquisition census and N13b acquisition contract. These are exact observed identities,
not a claim that every emitted issue represents a distinct product defect.

The full returned registry issue array has 409 unique complete-object identities; the full
audit has 431. Each was independently reconciled with an external `sort -u` over all JSON-line
identities; absent keys remain distinct from explicit null. Complete arrays, identity sets and
source denominators are preserved under `root/m1-probe-data`. The verdict does not depend on
the totals, and not every broader output-root finding was individually adjudicated. The concrete
missing GY audit registration and non-green GY audit decide the task.

**Removal/new-artifact probes.** In the disposable copy only, I removed the existing
`layer3_gy_composition_certificates.json` output registration, keeping its family and artifact
markers and producer intact. The complete finding identity set gains
`layer3_gy_artifact_not_registered` for that exact path, losing no baseline identities.
After restoring the registry, a new marked GY JSON in the Task-0 output directory adds that

user bypassing Git hooks or an unbounded proof about every possible artifact format.

GY family; lifecycle registration is incomplete (`surface_missing`). The gate exists and detects

## GY-D1 — `not_executed`

**Deciding result:** Two control constructors omit the catalog; the fetch persistence branch is a no-op.

**Task's exact plan text, read before implementation:** `policy-engine/docs/plans/active/layer3-slices/GY-engine-subordination.md`, lines 1800–1814.

> - **GY-D1 — Catalog → measurement-root producer.** wire-existing (catalog) + build-new
>   (root producer). Findings: F4. Wire `DatasetCatalogGraph` into Slice-0 `BIND` (and
>   later `ACQUIRE` once GY-E activates it), not `RetrievalService(dataset_catalog=None)`;
>   a real measurement-root producer so fetch writes a CAS artifact with producer-roots
>   (fix the `persist_payload` no-op). Done when: a pinned construct resolves through the
>   real catalog to a CAS-rooted artifact.
>   **Restated 2026-08-30 against a measurement, because the original prose is now half stale.**
>   `persist_payload` is **delivered** — `fabric/retrieval/executor.py:140` writes to CAS. Catalog
>   wiring is **1 of 3**: `runtime/quality/acquisition_planner.py:1320` passes `dataset_catalog=graph`,
>   while `runtime/http/services/control/nl_pipeline.py:5040` and `.../run_lifecycle.py:1340` pass none
>   and take the `None` default. Those two are the control lanes the promotion path runs through, which
>   is why `promotion_sequence.py` `_measurement_obligation` reports the measurement-rooted producer
>   owner **unwired**. Done when, restated: all three `RetrievalService` construction sites resolve a
>   real catalog, and a fixture removing the catalog from any one of them turns `GY-PR1`'s measurement
>   obligation red.

**Pre-measurement worksheet:** Completion requires every stated conjunct and applicable shared gate. A failing historical selected predicate may reproduce, pass, or be unmeasurable here; no current verdict is predicted from the standing label. The lane's more specific prediction, when recorded, follows.

**Done when, quoted before code inspection.** GY plan lines 1800–1814:

> Done when: a pinned construct resolves through the
> real catalog to a CAS-rooted artifact.
>
> Done when, restated: all three `RetrievalService` construction sites resolve a
> real catalog, and a fixture removing the catalog from any one of them turns `GY-PR1`'s measurement
> obligation red.

**Prediction.** I expected the historical split to remain: persistence delivered, catalog wiring
incomplete. **The persistence prediction was wrong.** A successful call of the real
`FetchExecutor.execute(..., persist_payload=True)` returns a metric but writes no CAS file.
The input connector is injected and deterministic; the executor, preview, fetch, quality branch,
and persistence branch are unchanged target code. This is a negative owner-path witness, not a
claim of real-network/catalog end-to-end success.

**Measurement.** `_build.gy_census.d1_probe` walks every tracked Python source file under `src/`
and reconciles the complete path set by Git and pathlib: 2,630 files, no unreadable file.
An alias-aware AST walk identifies direct named/attribute `RetrievalService` constructor calls;
independent full-file literal enumeration agrees on the exact call-site identities. There are
three such sites. Evaluating each unchanged call expression with the real service constructor
(only unrelated subcomponents replaced by inert fixtures) leaves `_dataset_catalog is None` at
`nl_pipeline.py:5040` and `run_lifecycle.py:1367`. The acquisition call at
`acquisition_planner.py:1378` supplies a catalog argument. Its probe object is a sentinel, so this
last observation establishes argument wiring, **not** real catalog resolution.

For persistence, the real imported executor runs after those constructor-fixture patches end.
Preview status is `ok`, the returned metric contains the fetched value, and complete independent
pathlib/os.walk inventories of the scratch CAS directory are both empty before and after.
`fabric/retrieval/executor.py:140–143` is still the explicit `_ = self._cas_root` no-op.

**What changed since the prior measurement?** The catalog omission remains at the current control
sites. More significantly, persistence was already a no-op at the historical measurement's
commit `73d930f8284682fafc283c2b78c54d64bbecf1dd` (2026-08-30). The executor bytes at that commit and
at the requested target are identical, with SHA-256
`6690526a6dd7f9e73a5be94f8687046777e997a671cae1600419dc2f55bd26ce`.
Thus the plan's “persist_payload is delivered” claim is contradicted at both endpoints; this
is not evidence of a new loss after August 30. Endpoint equality alone does not assert that no
intervening change/reversion ever occurred. The measurement-obligation owner itself has evolved:
current `promotion_sequence.py:5090–5122` consumes independently resolved, candidate/problem-bound
measurement evidence rather than the earlier blanket “owner unwired” wording. That does not
wire the missing construction-site catalogs.

**Deciding evidence.** The all-sites conjunct is false, independently of the persistence defect:
`bridge_missing` at the two control constructors. Persistence adds a measured `artifact_missing`
at this fetch owner. The prior data-forge measurement-root producer is a separate owner and may
write CAS; it cannot establish that this executor's `persist_payload` writes CAS. The required
GY-PR1 per-site removal fixture and remaining shared §3.5.5 conjuncts were not fully discharged;
they cannot rescue an already-false conjunct. No production change was made.

**Command and station.** At the common pinned worktree station:

```text
/Users/deniskopylov/polisyos/policy-engine/.venv/bin/python -m _build.gy_census.d1_probe
```

Receipt `root/d1-behavior-v2`: actual exit 0, 13.170 seconds, no timeout. Exit 0 means the probe
confirmed the documented failures; it does not mean D1 passed. The full stdout/stderr and
command/environment metadata are embedded with the receipt below. The initial probe used an
incorrect tracer fixture method and stopped before successful fetch; that setup error is retained
in `root/d1-behavior`, excluded from the persistence inference, and corrected only in scratch.
The independent Foundry reviewer re-read the probe, output and actual executor and confirmed
these boundaries. P01/P02/P29/P32/P36/P38 were rechecked; no repair attempted.

## GY-C1 — `not_executed`

**Deciding result:** Executable operation admission does not require the defined full adapter conformance.

**Task's exact plan text, read before implementation:** `policy-engine/docs/plans/active/layer3-slices/GY-engine-subordination.md`, lines 1847–1854.

> - **GY-C1 — Engines as Operations (adapters) + playbooks.** wire-existing. Findings:
>   F2. `LegacyNodeAdapter` lands incrementally, only for nodes needed by the active
>   playbook/operation under implementation (no 37-node mega-drop); each adapter declares
>   ports/preconditions/authority-transform as a Ring-1 hint; the three workflows →
>   `Playbook` trajectories the loop may deviate from; intent→operations (no
>   `workflow_id`). Done when: at least one playbook trajectory runs as a default
>   trajectory and the loop can deviate on a counterexample; adding another legacy node
>   follows the same adapter conformance test.

**Pre-measurement worksheet:** Completion requires every stated conjunct and applicable shared gate. A failing historical selected predicate may reproduce, pass, or be unmeasurable here; no current verdict is predicted from the standing label. The lane's more specific prediction, when recorded, follows.

**Verdict: `not_executed`.** The defined conformance-before-Operation-admission requirement is false at the measured live playbook/adapter seam; see `adjudication-C1-F1.md` for the operational-consumer chain and precise warrant. The counterexample-routing witness passes, and a repair terminal is not itself a violation. No candidate-to-authority escape is asserted.

Pin: `20082e545ba89cefc2fd913e1723f6ef7c63df39`. Prediction and exact shared requirements were recorded in `../inventory/census.json` before implementation inspection.

### Exact conjuncts and observed behavior

| Required property | Fresh observation | What it establishes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| At least one playbook trajectory runs as a default trajectory | Registry and intent routing tests pass. Both the recorded-input case and the existing stable-test case select `scientist_causal_full`; the loop attempts `phase2.estimate.run_causal_evaluation`, returns `repair_required`, and records `inputs.ukraine_foundry_method_input_bundle_ref` missing. | Default selection and a real adapter applicability attempt are established. A complete default trajectory is not demonstrated. A repair terminal alone is not a failure of the written condition. |
| Loop can deviate on a counterexample | Existing `test_workspace_loop_phase2_playbook_can_deviate_to_refine_blocker` passes. Explicit missing-bounds input produces `blocker-missing-bound`, a REFINE deviation and `search_ceiling_repair_required`. The real missing-input case also records a REFINE repair. | Typed counterexample routing is established. The explicit counterexample branch records no operation invocations; its trace is not evidence that a REFINE engine operation ran. The plan does not explicitly require such an operation in this conjunct. |
| Adding another legacy node follows the same adapter conformance test | Existing semantic-preservation checker rejects the removed-output node and accepts an adjacent producing node. The same live `_step_from_invocation` admits both as ESTIMATE playbook steps. | The semantic test exists and notices missing output. Its result is not consumed at this step-admission seam, which calls only the shape checker. Scope: two controlled nodes at the actual production step constructor, not an assertion about every possible registration path or a production authority escape. |

The shared admission rule is explicit, not inferred from a test: plan §3.5.3, lines 490–496 says adapter conformance criteria **all must hold before an engine asset is admitted as an Operation**, including `validate_adapter_preservation`, derived applicability, ports/transform, and a real-input smoke. Source `workspace/workflow_playbook_projection.py:283` calls only `validate_scientist_node_adapter_shape`; that function at `workspace/scientist_node_adapters.py:401` checks presence of contract structure. The separate output-preservation function at line 430 executes the node and detects its missing `causal_report_ref`. `C1-adapter-admission.json` preserves both returned steps and both semantic results. This observation supports a missing verification bridge at the measured admission seam; it does not conflate `validate_adapter_semantic_preservation` with the separate, explicitly named `adapter_contracts.validate_adapter_preservation` authority-field preservation API.

`C1-source-census.json` walks the complete `.py` denominator under `src/polisyos/runtime/quality/workspace/` and `tests/unit/runtime/quality/`: 186 files, every path and SHA recorded, zero syntax failures. Independent `ast.walk` and `NodeVisitor` occurrence sets agree. In this scoped set the semantic-preservation function has two callers, both tests; step construction calls the shape checker. This is a scoped fact, not a package-wide absence claim.

### Fixture and interpretation controls

The first recorded-input trace attempt encountered missing worktree-relative data. The data itself was locally accessible, so that failure was not retained as a product verdict. The completed trace run used the same pinned function code, temporarily changed only its module `__file__` data-root resolution in memory, and read the existing production parquet/manifest through `C1-data-root/production_data`. No semantic function was replaced. `C1-live-traces.json` records original source and function filenames, exact data paths, hashes and bytes. The recorded input still stops on the real missing adapter port; it is no longer stopped by absent data.

The default trace names BIND/REFINE/ESTIMATE/VERIFY, marks `build_literature_prior` and `reconcile_causal_graph` explicitly out of scope, and actually records only the attempted causal-evaluation adapter. The deliberate counterexample branch records BIND/ESTIMATE/REFINE in trace metadata but zero adapter invocations. These are distinct observations; the trace list is not recast as executed engine work.

### Shared §3.5.5 completion limits

Owner placement, predecessor fencing/default change, name-by-function and run-emitted/recomputed representative proof are conjuncts of completion, not discharged by the selected pytest result. This lane established the scoped conformance behavior and direct trace provenance. It did not establish a complete no-second-owner census, all predecessor/default guards, or a representative recomputed Phase-2 proof family. No complete-task GO, new source change, or task-standing edit is claimed.

### Undefined or unmeasurable as written

- **“Runs as a default trajectory”** does not state whether attempted execution followed by an honest repair terminal counts, or whether all default steps must execute. It does not require `frontier_stable`. The report supplies trace and invocation facts rather than silently selecting the stronger interpretation.
- **“Representative substrate”** in the shared proof gate has no declared population or representativeness criterion here. A complete representative-substrate claim cannot be measured from this text alone.
- Adapter conformance itself is defined by §3.5.3; the existence of a broken or missing fixture is not classified as an undefined requirement. “Another legacy node” provides no specific new-node witness, so the two controlled variants establish their scoped property, not a census of future additions.

### Final requirement-level adjudication


**Deciding requirement:** plan §3.5.3 at lines 490–495 requires that all listed conformance criteria hold **before an engine asset is admitted as an Operation**, including adapter preservation and a real-input smoke. This applies to C1's adapters-as-Operations and its “same adapter conformance test” clause. The literal local default/deviation conditions are not the deciding failure.

**The measured step is operational admission, not just a detached type constructor.** `_step_from_invocation` (`workflow_playbook_projection.py:263`) resolves a node from the registry, calls `ScientistNodeAdapter.from_node`, and returns a selected playbook step carrying the resulting operation and adapter identities. `from_node` constructs an `OperationContract` at `scientist_node_adapters.py:99`. The actual production consumer at `workspace/loop.py:1409` selects that registry's playbook and at lines 1448–1466 reconstructs its adapter under the same operation identity and calls `execute_candidate`, persisting its `OperationInvocationRecord` and candidate events. No intervening full conformance admission is present in that shown path. Registration in the separate Slice-0 `OperationRegistry` is not required for a Phase-2 engine asset to enter this executable operation trajectory.

The sole acceptance gate in the step constructor is `validate_scientist_node_adapter_shape` (`workflow_playbook_projection.py:283`), whose complete body checks contract-field presence and allowed execution kind. It neither runs an input smoke nor reads a prior preservation/smoke receipt. The completed controlled probe returns an admitted ESTIMATE step for a node that declares but does not produce `causal_report_ref`; the existing semantic-preservation owner returns `passed:false`, `output_not_preserved:causal_report_ref` for that same node. The adjacent producing control passes. Its rejection proves the separate semantic verifier works; the returned executable step and the actual consuming path prove that verifier result is not required at this admission seam. The explicitly named `adapter_contracts.validate_adapter_preservation` is not confused with this output-preservation function; the step constructor calls neither. One false required conformance-before-admission predicate is sufficient for `not_executed`.

**Scope:** controlled new-node substitution through the existing production step/adaptor path, with the actual downstream operation consumer verified by source. This does not claim candidate output obtained authority or that every possible registry path is broken. Typed reason: `required_conformance_not_consumed_at_operation_admission`; capability label `bridge_missing`.

The existing deviation test passes. A repair terminal is not failure merely because a test expected `frontier_stable`. Whether a partly attempted/default trajectory counts as “runs” remains a separate textual ambiguity; it does not rescue the independently false conformance requirement.

See `adjudication-C1-F1.md`. No failed-workflow authority escape was observed.

Pin: `20082e545ba89cefc2fd913e1723f6ef7c63df39`. Prediction and shared requirements were recorded in `../inventory/census.json` before implementation inspection.

### Complete named surface denominator

The task names `run`, `artifact`, `lineage`, `export`, `dashboard`, `public packet`; the worker/job-result condition adds one distinct layer. The canonical owner `check_layer3_workflow_failure_authority.py:29` lists the same six surface classes. `F1-owned-http-observations.json` preserves every readback and actual HTTP response body, with a separate complete-job negative. No route-class denominator is inferred from a single observed member.

| Surface/layer | Actual measured path | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| run | `ControlPlaneService.get_job_status` | state `failed`, `repair_required`, consumed boundary and blocked authority; direct HTTP job-route negative also passes |
| artifact | GET artifact content | 409, actual body `authority_surface_admission_blocked` |
| lineage | GET artifact lineage | 409, actual body `authority_surface_admission_blocked` |
| export | GET artifact export | 409, actual body `authority_surface_admission_blocked` |
| dashboard | POST artifact render, after valid indexed ownership | 409, actual body `authority_surface_admission_blocked` |
| public packet | `build_public_export_bundle` | raises `PublicExportRedactionError`, code `authority_surface_blocked` |
| worker/job result | durable failure plus direct `complete_job` negative | observed state `failed`; attempted clean completion refused |

The packet assertions were not substituted for route behavior: the HTTP bodies show the actual composed authority decision and boundary reference for all four HTTP artifact surfaces. A separate read-only wrapper merely recorded original request results.

### Canonical-check failure and controlled follow-up

The unchanged canonical command `check_layer3_workflow_failure_authority.py --check --output-format json` exits 1 at `run_lifecycle.py:3386`: its `legacy_shadow_candidate` fixture constructs a natural-language request with neither model field supplied. Both fields default to None, and the pinned admission path requires a nonempty request model list. A separate direct capture records the typed exception exactly: `RuntimeHTTPError`, status 422, `llm_model_unconfigured`, and `extensions` explicitly null. It never reaches that scenario's surface probes. This is a verification-path failure, not an observed authority leak, and not fresh evidence for the older `FrozenInstanceError` wording.

The canonical failed-workflow scenario itself runs. Its original render request returned 403 `authorization_binding_artifact_unscoped`: CAS owner metadata exists, but render authorization obtains ownership from finalized Core-run indexing. That 403 is a real denial; however, it does not exercise the authority predicate. Treating “not 409” as a leaking surface would be a proxy verdict.

The additional fixture used only existing `RunContext.start`, `add_output`, and `finalize(status='fail')` in scratch to give the **identical failed-progress artifact bytes** a real indexed tenant owner. No authorization bypass, runtime repair or authority-field change was made. The progress artifact remained `sha256:0faa684ad41f5365388687d6d5adfbe2fd73b989fec7f96322585bdb5e4125b2`. The unchanged render route then reached its authority gate and returned the actual 409 refusal above. The ownership setup and complete before/after responses are retained separately.

Three focused worker/HTTP-job tests pass. An additional existing legacy-shadow workflow test also passes: a legacy success claiming `decision_admissible` is reduced to `candidate_only`, its quality remains `fail`, and its six-surface packet consumes the downgraded boundary. This closes the available workflow candidate witness without pretending that the canonical legacy **NL** proof scenario succeeded.

### Shared §3.5.5 completion limits

The canonical two-scenario proof-family recomputation is still not green and no governed proof was regenerated. The direct fail-closed measurements are fresh; they do not establish all owner-placement, predecessor/default or full generated-proof-family requirements. The legacy proof's hardcoded deterministic UUID/time fixture is also not asserted here to satisfy the shared real-run-time language. Representativeness clauses principally govern search/recall/precision closure; an unspecified benchmark population is not treated as an additional F1 requirement or a reason for its verdict. Capability label for this incomplete closeout is **verification_missing**, not consumer_missing or a demonstrated authority leak.

### Undefined or unmeasurable as written

- **“All probed surfaces”** does not itself fix a route/member denominator. The body resolves six named surface classes plus worker, which this lane measured; it does not enumerate every endpoint/format/audience within each class.
- **“Visibly downgraded”** gives no complete allowed encoding. This run used the unambiguous blocked/refused branch, so that undefined alternative does not prevent measuring its failed-workflow witness.
- The original 403 ownership failure and 422 empty-model-request failure are concrete fixture/verification limitations, not reasons to label the literal failed-workflow condition unmeasurable as written.

### Final requirement-level adjudication


**Deciding requirement:** §3.5.4 lines 562–567 requires packets to be written by the real run and recomputed by their validator; §3.5.5 lines 608–609 expressly says “validators recompute”; lines 1716–1720 make this part of every task's Done when. This is an executable, defined proof obligation, not a demand to perform an unspecified census.

The canonical proof family is committed as `architecture/policy_design_case/layer3_gy_workflow_failure_authority_proofs.json`, names `proof_source=durable_worker_surface_readback_recompute`, and contains both `workflow_failure` and `legacy_shadow_candidate`. Its producer builds both unconditionally at validator lines 117–120 before it can return the proof or perform the drift comparison. The preserved fresh `--check` command exits 1 at the second scenario; direct error capture records 422 `llm_model_unconfigured`.

**Source adjudication removes the environment ambiguity.** This is not merely a missing external model in the measuring station: the canonical request at validator lines 210–217 supplies neither `llm_model` nor `llm_models`; both fields have unconditional `None` defaults in `core/contracts/control.py:369–370`, with no model-filling validator in that DTO. `launch_nl_run` derives its model list only from those request fields and raises the named error when the list is empty (`run_lifecycle.py:3380–3389`). The canonical fixed request therefore cannot produce its committed second proof under the pinned source. No external model configuration can fill fields this request leaves None along that code path. The complete live rederivation required by P29 is false, rather than merely not attempted. Typed reason: `canonical_proof_recompute_false`; capability label `verification_missing`.

The clock is separately fixed by the validator at lines 178–182, and both committed proofs carry the authored `2026-06-16T14:15:16+00:00`; the plan's real-time requirement at §3.5.5 lines 608–609 is an additional concern, but the verdict does **not** need a ruling about deterministic fixture clocks. The already decisive canonical rederivation failure suffices.

The literal failed-workflow behavior holds across the six named surface classes plus worker after valid fixture ownership, and the separate legacy-workflow candidate test passes. This is useful positive evidence and remains recorded. It does not satisfy the mandatory generated-proof recomputation conjunct, so it does not make the complete task `executed`. Neither the original render403 nor the absence of an unrelated owner census is used as the deciding failure.

## GY-M2 — `executed`

**Deciding result:** Actual tourism selection works; the unchanged semantic test rejects selector removal.

**Task's exact plan text, read before implementation:** `policy-engine/docs/plans/active/layer3-slices/GY-engine-subordination.md`, lines 1934–1938.

> - **GY-M2 — GX reducer case-parameterization.** extend-existing. Finding: F14.
>   Parameterize the GX reducer CLI / `data_home` for arbitrary case input so the tourism
>   slice — not only the pinned ua-msme — validates. Runs before GY-L / GY-V (which
>   validate non-pinned cases). Done when: the GX validator runs on the tourism case, not
>   only the pinned ua-msme `data_home`.

**Pre-measurement worksheet:** Completion requires every stated conjunct and applicable shared gate. A failing historical selected predicate may reproduce, pass, or be unmeasurable here; no current verdict is predicted from the standing label. The lane's more specific prediction, when recorded, follows.

**Done when, quoted before code inspection.** GY plan lines 1934–1938:

> - **GY-M2 — GX reducer case-parameterization.** extend-existing. Finding: F14.
>   Parameterize the GX reducer CLI / `data_home` for arbitrary case input so the tourism
>   slice — not only the pinned ua-msme — validates. Runs before GY-L / GY-V (which
>   validate non-pinned cases). Done when: the GX validator runs on the tourism case, not
>   only the pinned ua-msme `data_home`.

**Prediction.** I expected a case-labelled CLI with a pinned implementation. **That prediction
was wrong.** The actual tourism parameterization works and the existing semantic test detects
its removal. The historical “tourism returns zero hits” rationale is contradicted by code that
already existed before the claimed August measurement.

**Measurement.** The production CLI runs `--case tourism --check` and returns the GX diagnostic
status `expected_red`, exit 1. Its exit policy at
`check_policy_design_case_layer3_gx_hardening.py:2425` returns zero only for `pass`. That is a
separate property from M2's case parameterization; M2 does not promise the absence of GX findings.
No GX finding was repaired or waived.

The exact existing test
`tests/repo_quality/tools/test_policy_design_case_layer3_gx_hardening.py::test_gx_validator_case_selector_runs_real_tourism_case`
runs complete real validators for both cases. It checks the actual requested construct identity
sets, distinct route replay keys and final hashes, tourism-specific artifact references, and
absence of the pinned ua-msme identity from the **entire serialized tourism report**. It passes.
The selector owner is `proving_ground/pinned_route_demand_home.py:698–745`; the CLI passes its
selection into the existing GX reducer via a scoped ContextVar (`...gx_hardening.py:312–328`).
The existing data-home owner loads the selected typed request, aliases, scopes and demand;
the reducer emits case-specific reports and proof hashes.

**Removal probe.** In a disposable process I replaced only the selector behavior with “ignore
the supplied case/data_home and select ua-msme.” The signature, names, registry, source markers
and artifacts remain. The same unchanged test executes the real complete validator twice and
rejects the tourism call returning the ua-msme case. Its fresh baseline passes and its removed
property fails: this is behavioral enforcement, not a marker check. The probe captures full
returned reports and exact invocation records; it does not compare mere finding totals.

**What changed since the prior measurement?** Independent local-history review compared the
validator, test, selector owner and case registry between the August 30 measurement commit
`73d930f8284682fafc283c2b78c54d64bbecf1dd` and the target: no byte delta in this selected mechanism
set. The CLI selector and explicit tourism test were introduced by
`584bd7b72deb74694db87f4612176be0cb78724f` on June 28. The old absence claim was already inconsistent
with those files. This is not a claim that the historical runtime test passed; the runtime pass
reported here is fresh.

**Shared hygiene.** This extends the existing GX reducer and its single data-home owner. Keeping
the ua-msme default is intentional and compatible with the task; no replacement or subordinated
predecessor needs a StrangleReceipt for this selector extension. The current test exercises the
actual case inputs, producer-root/reducer output path and recomputed final hash, and the negative
probe detects loss of selection. An independent review found no concrete missing shared-hygiene
conjunct for this bounded extension. This verdict does not grant authority to the underlying GX
expected-red findings, close GY-L, or claim a live network/production policy outcome.

That is GY-DEF23's class one slice deeper: a vacuous refusal is honest, a caller-asserted True MINTS. Separately _coupling_obligation refuses on two tokens NO PRODUCER EMITS, so COUPLING passes for every design. Three vacuous passes, two vacuous fails. AND THE REASON NOBODY LOOKED: test_scope_insufficient_obligation_does_not_vacuously_pass uses EFFECT and MEASUREMENT - the permanent failures - as its vehicle for the fail-closed property, so they read as deliberate red controls; the system had a quiet incentive not to fix them. GY-K's ambiguous row is RESOLVED by the same experiment, not by adjudication: grounding_relation.py documents AxisEntailmentWitness as 'GY-K-style ... input, never as decider' on an optional field, and GroundingRelationCertificate declares shadow_only and no_bind_admit_promote - so GY-K does produce entailment witnesses and that lineage is architecturally forbidden from deciding anything. Ambiguous 3 -> 2, executed 47 -> 48. GY-PR1's scope GREW: wire MEASUREMENT, orchestrate EVAL_SAFETY, rule and implement EFFECT/ADMISSIBILITY, repair three vacuous passes, and take the three as its red controls. NO CODE WAS TOUCHED, deliberately: _gate_outcome_hash hashes the full obligation records, so owner_ref and obligation_class both enter it and even correcting a misleading owner STRING is receipt-affecting - this is a governed n9_obligation_scope.v1 -> .v2 bump behind a per-task plan, never a drive-by edit.         "text": "  model / obligation / calibration scope) that freezes promotion for the affected scope. Done when:\n  crossing an L3 amendment or an L5 schema-regime changepoint marks dependent certificates stale and\n  forces revalidation before they can stay on the decision front; a high OpenWorldRisk scope freezes\n  promotion; a stale certificate cannot appear in a public result. **Universality rider (Rev 15,\n  §3.5.8):** epoch boundaries are **derived from the full substrate data** — every L5 `schema_regime`\n  entry and every L3 amendment window in the registry (U3): a new domain's regime added via data\n  alone creates epoch semantics with **zero engine code**; the ukraine v1-prewar/v2-wartime\n  changepoint is the **first test case, never an enum in engine code**; the revision-trigger\n  vocabulary stays the typed generic list (it already is — keep it that way); a scope with no\n  regime/amendment data gets honest `epoch_scope_unresolved`, not an assumed epoch (U4).\n  **Acquisition-epoch rider (Rev 16):** N13b acquisition events (a new dataset version / source\n  watermark / overlay epoch) are **live epoch-boundary sources** alongside L3 amendments and L5\n  schema regimes — the world growing IS a model-revision trigger: certificates whose evidence\n  predates an admitted acquisition in their scope become `revalidation_required` exactly like an\n  amendment crossing. The N13b overlay epoch stamps and the N12 epoch manager share ONE time\n  semantics (no fragmentation — the time-semantics anti-pattern); and **derived artifacts\n  inherit epoch validity from their inputs (Rev 17, §3.5.12-D6)** — an input revision (agencies\n  revise series) marks dependent derivations `revalidation_required`, and because the\n  derivation certificate IS the recipe, revalidation is an automatic recompute.\n  **Post-publication perturbation cascade rider (Rev 18, distillation §6.5 · M36/M25):**\n  incidents, appeals, corrections, retractions, legal changes and discovered bias are\n  **distinct** revision-trigger classes, not one \"reopen\" — each is authoritative only for\n  `review_required`/`contested`/annotation **until adjudicated**, then bounded to\n  `annotation_only`/`invalidate`/`reissue`/`supersede`/`withdraw` (a single upheld appeal is\n  instance-scope, not class-scope; a renumbered rule with an unchanged logic-hash is\n  `annotation_only`, not supersession). A closed case is **never silently mutated** — it stays\n  replay-valid under its closure epoch and gets a superseding/reissue link. Source-status\n  invalidity propagates as a replayable `EvidenceValidityEvent` (source → evidence-line → claim →\n  publication) — no authority survives after its support is lost. Reuse `case_lifecycle` +\n  `core.contracts.rule_evolution` + `scientist/governance/continuous`\n  (`incident`/`invalidation`/`reissue`/`lifecycle_bridge`); do **not** build a parallel owner.\n  **P29 rider:** the δ-accounting this epoch layer gates is complete only **relative to the declared\n  obligation set** — OpenWorldRisk must carry that conditional; an unconditional \"risk ≤ δ\" is\n  false (this is the INT-R1 obligation-completeness dependency, not a solved property).\n  **Missed-obligation reissue rider (Rev 25, ratified `INT-K01`/`INT-K02`; extends the P29 rider\n  above from a caveat into a trigger).** \"Obligation-completeness alarm\" is already in this task's\n  revision-trigger list; the ratified kernel fixes what the alarm *means* and what the cascade must\n  preserve. An obligation discovered **after** issuance is not evidence that the earlier arithmetic\n  was miscomputed — under `INT-K01` completeness was only ever relative to a **declared basis**, so\n  discovery moves the basis rather than falsifying the computation. The cascade is therefore\n  challenge → invalidation → **new epoch** → reissue under the widened basis, append-only: the\n  superseded certificate stays **historically reproducible under its own closure epoch and its own\n  declared set**, while its **current authority is withdrawn**. Never rewrite the old numbers to\n  match the new basis — that would destroy the evidence of what was known when, and it is the\n  append-only law (`S0-K08`) applied to coverage. Under `INT-K02` every reissued statement carries\n  the widened declared set and the relative-basis rider visibly; a `delta` that changed only because\n  the basis widened must not be projectable as a *better* result.\n  **Release-family transcript rider (Rev 26, ratified `PV-K07`; see `GY-GAP3`).** The controlled\n  release-family transcript that `PV-K07` presupposes is **the same append-only shape this task\n  already owns** for epochs: declared membership, chronology, current heads, append-only correction,\n  and no rewrite of a superseded result.       "text": "### 3.5.5 Phase-0–2 implementation-review corrections — strangle, owner-first, name-by-function, emit-proof (P27/P28/P29/P30)\n\nThe phase-0–2 review found three recurring build-hygiene failures (now register patterns\nP27/P28/P29). They are binding on every remaining task: a task may not close while\nre-creating one. **P28 (strangle) is load-bearing** — without it the universal loop\nbecomes \"one more layer over the static DAG\" instead of its replacement, which is the\nwhole point of the slice.\n\n**A. Concrete debts to clear while fixing phases 0–2** (each move is owner-first +\nstrangle, not a new parallel file):\n\n| Debt found in the partial build | Pattern | Correct move |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| `Slice0SearchLedger` (`gy_loop.py`) beside canonical `SearchLedger` (`pdc/_impl/layer2_design_search.py`) | P27 | DONE first pass: `Slice0SearchLedger` extends canonical `SearchLedger`; remaining cleanup is to narrow GY sidecar fields as consumers migrate. |\n| Second `AcquisitionPlanner` (`gy_loop.py`) beside `acquisition_planner.py` / `layer2_substrate_acquisition.py` | P27 | DONE first pass: GY-E delegates routing/disposition to `plan_requirement_gap_acquisition`; remaining cleanup is to move the thin façade out of `gy_loop.py`. |\n| Lex-bounds rule duplicated in `gy_spine_repair.py` and `policy_design/search.py` | P27 | DONE first pass: one owner = the engine (`search.py`); GY façade calls it. |\n| Two fixture catalog graphs (`_InMemorySlice0CatalogGraph` + `build_slice0_fixture_catalog_graph`) | P27 | DONE: one fixture builder over the real `DatasetCatalogGraph`; tests use the canonical builder. |\n| `require_explicit_parameter_bounds=False` default still launders `None→0.0` | P28 | DONE first pass: default is explicit-bounds fail-closed; remaining legacy inferred-bounds calls must stay explicit until deleted. |\n| 2674-line `gy_loop.py` holding B/D1/D2/D3/E/H | P27 (dual) | Move each gate/producer to its owning module; `gy_loop.py` keeps only the loop. |\n| `ProductionLoopRunProof` hand-authored, shape-only validator | P29 | DONE: emitted from durable worker path and validator recomputes from CAS/index refs. |\n| F4/F7 \"closed\" on a 2-record catalog corpus | P29 | Measure recall/precision on a representative corpus, or mark `surface_out_of_scope` with rationale. |\n\n**B. Strangle protocol (P28).** A replace/subordinate task is not done until, **in the\nsame change**, it (1) deletes or fences the predecessor, (2) flips the default to the\ncorrected path, and (3) adds a guard (lint/test) that fails if a new caller reaches the\npredecessor. It then persists a `StrangleReceipt` (§3.5.4) with a recomputing validator.\nLegacy that genuinely cannot be cut yet is fenced as `legacy_shadow` / candidate-only\n**and** listed in `remaining_callers` with a dated cut ticket — never left as a silent\ndefault. This is exactly how GY-B2 already treats `/runs`, `/runs/nl`, and the\n`workflow_run` job path; every later subordination (GY-C1 legacy nodes, GY-C2 lex/\ngovernance, GY-F1 worker surfaces) follows the same pattern, not an additive layer.\n\n**C. Owner-first protocol (P27).** Before `class Foo` or a new `gy_*.py`, consult the\n§3.5.2 ownership map and run `grep -rl \"<concept-root>\" src/polisyos/{pdc/_impl,runtime/quality}`\nfor a live owner. If one exists, extend it. New files are for genuinely-new orchestration\ncontracts only. Free-growth still holds (§3.5.3): a correctly added engine asset becomes an\nOperation with zero new code — if you are writing a hand-maintained list or a parallel\ngate, stop.\n\n**D. Emit-proof protocol (P29).** See the §3.5.4 P29 note: identifiers come from the run\n(no placeholders), times are real, validators recompute, and any search/recall/precision\nclosure is measured on a representative substrate — not a fixture small enough to make the\nmetric vacuous. A committed Slice-0 `Slice0FixtureManifest` is allowed (§3.5.1); a\n2-record corpus standing in for the *benchmark substrate* of an F4/F7 closure is not.\n\n**E. Name-by-function protocol (P30) — so reuse is self-evident.** New files are named for\nthe capability they own (`workspace_loop.py`, not `gy_loop.py`); the owner-first grep (C)\nis by *function word*, so it only finds owners if files are function-named. The phase-0–2\n`gy_*` files are a standing P30 debt: either rename each to its function, or — where it\nholds genuinely-new orchestration — add a module docstring that names the canonical owners\nit extends (`SearchLedger`, `acquisition_planner`, `adapter_contracts`, `semantic_binding`,\n`data_forge_binding`) and links related modules, so the next implementer reads them before\nwriting a parallel file. No new GY file may take a bare plan-provenance name without that\nbreadcrumb. Naming is not cosmetic: it decides which file the next person opens first, and\nis the cheapest defense against re-creating P27.\n\n**F. Standing gate for phases 2→5.** Every task's `Done when` now also requires: no second\nlive owner for any concept it touches (P27); a `StrangleReceipt` for any path it replaces,\nwith the default flipped (P28); function-named modules with owner breadcrumbs, never a bare\nplan name (P30); and run-emitted, recomputed proof packets on a representative substrate\n(P29). Checked at design review and at closeout, alongside the matrix/GX gates. A task whose\nlocal tests pass but that leaves a parallel owner, an un-strangled default, a plan-named\nfile with no owner breadcrumb, or an authorial proof is **not done**.\n"
    },

A task that leaves a parallel owner, an un-strangled legacy\ndefault, or an authorial proof is **not done**, regardless of local test status."

    "lift_resolution_binding_gates": {
      "path": "policy-engine/docs/plans/active/layer3-slices/GY-engine-subordination.md",
      "first_line": 633,
      "last_line": 671,
      "text": "### 3.5.6 Substrate / binding lift completeness gates (the GY-S lesson — binding for every lift / resolution / binding task)\n\nThe GY-S substrate lifts (S1 data-state, S2 knowledge, S3 intervention) cost many adversarial\nrounds because each shipped a **shell** that passed its own narrow probes: coverage looked green but\non a curated subset; authority was **supplied, not derived**; the contract exercised only the\nhappy-path. The failure **escaped one level deeper each round** — for S3 the supplied authority went\ncaller-supplied → hardcoded code-table → hand-injected into git-ignored data → relocated into a\ntracked JSON the runtime merely *trusted*; for S2 it was percent-only units / single-row lineage /\nweight-synthetic contested. The disposition is always the same: **derive through the real owner +\nvalidate (fail-closed on a fake input), never supply; be generic over the data, not enumerated; and\nmake the gate exercise the decisive property.** Four gates are now **binding on every task that\nlifts, resolves, or binds authority** (the GY-S block and the cycle tasks N2/N4/N7/N8/N9 — their\ncontracts must encode all four for their decisive property):\n\n1. **Full-denominator coverage.** Measure coverage against the **full real vocabulary** (count the\n   real source files / registries), never a curated subset or a 2-record corpus. A green `N/N` is\n   load-bearing only when `N` is the full real denominator — prove the denominator (`P10`).\n2. **Fail-closed on a fake / novel input.** A binding to a **non-existent owner target** (a slot not\n   in the real world model / `GlobalState`, a provision not in real L3), an unknown unit, or an\n   out-of-domain parameter **must fail closed**. This proves the runtime **validates through the\n   real owner**, not merely trusts a declared / curated / supplied value (`P32`, the\n   resolve→content-bind→validate root). A tracked binding artifact is legitimate **only** if it is\n   owner-validated this way — a JSON the runtime trusts is just a relocated name-map.\n3. **Data-only free-grow.** A genuinely **new** entry (knob / law / family / claim / threshold)\n   added via **data alone** must lift with **zero code change**; a malformed one fails closed. This\n   proves the mechanism is **generic over the data**, not an enumerated / name-substring branch\n   (Rule 12, `P31`). Reusing an existing mechanism for the \"novel\" case is a fake free-grow.\n4. **The contract mutates the DECISIVE validation property (`P29`).** The behavioral contract must\n   include a remove-the-property mutation for the **decisive** property — the fail-closed-on-fake\n   owner validation of gate 2 — not only coverage / free-grow / no-hardcode. The gate must go **red**\n   if owner-validation is removed while the happy-path bindings stay valid. A runtime that is correct\n   today but whose contract would not catch that regression is **not done** (this is the exact\n   verifier-completeness gap that held S3 to its last round).\n\nEvery impl/audit prompt and every `Done when` for a lift/resolution/binding task front-loads these\nfour — so the implementer builds to them on the first pass instead of rediscovering them through\nrounds. Verification stays **targeted** (§Commands; blast-radius + recomputing validators + ruff +\nguardrails), never full pytest.\n"
    },
    "adapter_conformance": {
      "path": "policy-engine/docs/plans/active/layer3-slices/GY-engine-subordination.md",
      "first_line": 483,
      "last_line": 498,
      "text": "### 3.5.3 Operation-discovery sources + conformance criteria (anti-hidden-table)\n\n\"Discovered, not enumerated\" (Rule 12) is only real if the sources and admission\ncriteria are concrete and the no-hardcode lint bites. **First discovery sources:**\nfoundry method registry (`get_registry().list_all()` — 389 methods), fabric connector\nregistry (`PROFILE_ID_BY_CONNECTOR_ID` + connector discovery), `scientist/agent` tool\nregistry (KnowledgeToolkit/tools), `data_forge` catalog (`DatasetCatalogGraph`), `ir`\nanalytics contracts (port vocabulary). **Adapter conformance criteria** (all must hold\nbefore an engine asset is admitted as an Operation): (1) a typed signature is\ndiscoverable from the registry (input_slots/dtypes/`requires`); (2) it passes\n`validate_adapter_preservation` + the derived formal-applicability check; (3) it declares\n`consumes`/`produces` ports + an `authority_transform`; (4) a smoke runs it on a real\ninput (executable, not merely registered). **Free-growth test (Rule 12):** a correctly\nadded engine asset becomes an Operation with **zero new code**; any hand-maintained\noperation/method/construct list is a lint failure to mark→replace→delete.\n"
    },
    "required_proof_packets": {
      "path": "policy-engine/docs/plans/active/layer3-slices/GY-engine-subordination.md",
      "first_line": 499,
      "last_line": 568,
      "text": "### 3.5.4 Required proof packets (anti-P01/P05/P08/P10/P25)\n\nThe following packets are not optional prose reports. Each named high-risk task must\npersist the packet as a generated artifact with a recomputing validator. The packet is\nthe acceptance surface: reviewers should inspect fields, not only task summaries.\n\n- **`ProductionLoopRunProof`** (GY-B2/GY-L/GY-V2): `{run_id, job_id, endpoint,\n  job_kind, enqueued_at, worker_lease_id, worker_id, _execute_workflow_invocation_id,\n  workspace_loop_invocation_id, control_store_state_transitions, input_artifacts,\n  output_search_exit_contract_ref, output_cas_refs, artifacts_index_refs,\n  surface_reads_checked, legacy_path_disposition}`. Required path:\n  `enqueue_job -> ControlWorker -> _execute_workflow -> WorkspaceLoop -> CAS +\n  artifacts_index + /runs readback`. A direct helper call does not satisfy this proof.\n- **`Slice0FixtureManifest`** (GY-B/GY-D1/GY-H): `{fixture_id,\n  construct_scope_query, jurisdiction, population, time_horizon,\n  expected_catalog_binding_refs, expected_connector_profile,\n  expected_producer_root_kind, expected_terminal, forbidden_terminals,\n  negative_controls}`. The manifest is the committed source of truth for Slice-0\n  fixture expectations; implementation may not replace it with an inline fixture table\n  or a prose \"World-Bank style\" label.\n- **`AuthorityDerivationTrace`** (GY-A2/GY-B/GY-V4): `{operation_invocation_id,\n  output_artifact_ref, declared_authority_transform, computed_evidence_kind,\n  computed_decision_grade, producer_root_classes, method_classification,\n  applicability_result_ref, calibration_refs, counterexamples_closed,\n  certified_envelope_ref, unresolved_blockers, resulting_authority_boundary_ref,\n  transform_mismatch_disposition}`. This is the audit trail for `A.verify`; an\n  Operation-declared transform is an input hint only and cannot be the stamped result.\n- **`AuthorityCandidateInventory`** (GY-F3/GY-V4): one row per candidate-positive\n  status, including `{producer_component, source_artifact_ref, field_path, status_text,\n  candidate_positive_rule, firewall_name, exclusion_reason, resulting_boundary_ref,\n  false_exclusion_review, reviewer, reviewed_at}`. The count must reconcile to 406 on\n  the Task-0 baseline, and false exclusions must become explicit repair tickets.\n- **`CASIntegrityReport`** (GY-F2/GY-V5): `{artifact_ref, payload_digest,\n  canonicalization_rule_ref, blob_uri, manifest_ref, authority_manifest_ref,\n  duplicate_group_id, referrers, report_index_refs, lineage_refs, tamper_probe_result,\n  mutation_probe_result, gc_retain_reason, gc_dry_run_result}`. It must prove digest\n  semantics, dedup, mutation/tamper rejection, and GC survivability.\n- **`TimeSourceEnvelopeAudit`** (GY-F3/GY-V5): `{catalog_watermark,\n  source_observed_at, source_published_at, source_updated_at, ingested_at,\n  effective_time, legal_valid_time, transaction_time, as_of_time, replay_time,\n  run_started_at, run_finished_at, node_started_at, node_finished_at,\n  retention_or_expiry, mismatch_disposition}`. A mismatch must block, downgrade, or\n  create an obligation; it cannot be logged as decoration.\n- **`SecretAndPIIScanReport`** (GY-F2/GY-V4): scopes are `{DAG bundles, connector\n  request/response payloads, CAS manifests, raw artifact content/download routes,\n  dashboard/public/export packets}`. Records include `{scope, artifact_ref_or_route,\n  detector_version, finding_kind, redaction_applied, authority_surface_blocked,\n  negative_fixture_result}`.\n- **`SemanticBenchmarkRun`** (GY-D3/GY-V3): `{benchmark_ref, benchmark_version,\n  label_owner, reviewer, rule_version_ref, construct_scope, queries, returned_hits,\n  precision_at_k, recall_at_known_seeds, known_seeds_missed, negative_controls_passed,\n  threshold_disposition}`. The gate consumes this packet; it may not validate itself.\n- **`VOISelectionAudit`** (GY-H/GY-I/GY-V4): `{workspace_id, cycle_index,\n  candidate_actions, agent_suggested_scores, normalized_scores, deterministic_voi_inputs,\n  rejected_or_clipped_inputs, selected_action, reason, authority_gain_basis,\n  decision_value_basis, cost_basis, bias_probe_result}`. Agent estimates are Ring-1\n  candidates; GY-H owns the deterministic normalization and selection decision.\n- **`StrangleReceipt`** (every replace/subordinate task — see §3.5.5): `{predecessor_ref,\n  replacement_ref, disposition: deleted|fenced_default_flipped, default_before,\n  default_after, guard_ref, remaining_callers, remaining_callers_disposition, removed_loc,\n  verified_by}`. It proves the predecessor was cut or fenced and the default flipped in the\n  same change (P28). \"Both paths reachable\" or \"zero deletions\" fails the receipt.\n\n**P29 — these packets are emitted, not authored.** Every packet above must be written by\nthe real run it claims and its validator must recompute it from live code/artifacts and\nfail on drift. The phase-0 `ProductionLoopRunProof` was hand-authored with placeholder ids\nand a shape-only validator — the exact `authorial-refs` laundering (F12) these packets\nexist to prevent. A packet whose identifiers are round/placeholder, whose times are\n`…T00:00:00Z`, or whose validator only checks shape, does **not** satisfy its task.\n"
    },

      "text": "## 11. Acceptance bar\n\n- The two-ring waist (17 waist contracts, roughly 13 new and the rest reused/extended\n  per §3.5.2) is\n  wired; **Ring-2 fields are not agent-writable (field-level, enforced + tested)**;\n  `pdc` never imports engines; the `AuthorityBoundary` lattice tests cover\n  `authoritative_for`, `may_not_use_for`, envelope intersection, `evidence_kind`\n  partial meet, and `decision_grade` total meet; `AuthorityDerivationTrace` proves\n  `A.verify` derives the stamped boundary independently from operation hints.\n- The control loop runs both Slice-0 fixtures end-to-end **via the durable production\n  trigger (GY-B2)** to typed `SearchExitContract`s with `FrontierSnapshot`,\n  `SearchLedger`, replay levels A/B/C, and persisted `ProductionLoopRunProof`s showing\n  `enqueue_job -> ControlWorker -> _execute_workflow -> WorkspaceLoop -> CAS/index ->\n  /runs readback`; failed/legacy-shadow jobs cannot complete as authority-looking\n  clean successes.\n- Every coverage-matrix row a task acts on moves off `bridge_missing`/`surface_missing`/\n  `absent` to a complete chain **with a semantic test** (the matrix is the progress meter).\n- The binding constraint is real: a pinned construct resolves through the real catalog to\n  a CAS-rooted measurement artifact with a `CertifiedOperationEnvelope`; recall@seeds +\n  freshness recorded; non-execution-ready connectors fail closed; the groundable\n  Slice-0 fixture is driven by `Slice0FixtureManifest`, reaches a measurement-rooted\n  `grounded_partial_admissible` **Estimate-port** outcome, and is explicitly forbidden\n  from emitting `grounded_admissible` or promoting a `DesignCandidate`; the tourism\n  ceiling fixture stops honestly.\n- `grounded_abstention` is emitted only past the domain-vs-search-ceiling gate; else\n  `search_ceiling_repair_required` (F1/F8); simultaneous terminal triggers follow the\n  §8.6 precedence.\n- No authority surface renders/exports/signs a failed or candidate workflow as authority;\n  no scoped secret/PII leak across raw routes, DAG bundles, connector payloads, CAS\n  manifests, dashboard/public/export packets; CAS loop outputs carry `manifest.authority`\n  and pass digest/dedup/tamper/GC survivability checks; S12 refs dereference or are\n  candidate-only; the 406 candidate-positive statuses reconcile to a reviewed\n  `AuthorityCandidateInventory`.\n- A `PolicyProgram` is never promoted without a `CompositionCertificate`; feedback\n  decomposition is rejected; emergent claims are capped to their own grounding.\n- Graded outcomes route partial evidence to `grounded_partial_admissible` (GY-J), moving\n  `useful_design_rate` off 0 honestly without weakening floors.\n- The GY/loop artifact family has a registered lifecycle (F18); the GX validator runs on\n  a non-pinned case (F14); every GY artifact passes the GX hardening validator; the Task\n  0 coverage matrix and audit suite stay green.\n- No parallel engine/pipeline/agent/DataNeed-type was built; engines entered only as\n  Operations (adapters); the three workflows are playbooks, not modes.\n- **Build hygiene (P27/P28/P29/P30):** no GY concept has two live owners (the §3.5.2 owner\n  map is clean — `SearchLedger`, `AcquisitionPlanner`, the lex-bounds rule, and the fixture\n  catalog each have exactly one home); modules are named by function with owner breadcrumbs,\n  not by plan (`gy_loop.py`→`workspace_loop.py`, or a docstring naming the owners it extends\n  — P30); every subordination/replacement task shipped a `StrangleReceipt` with the\n  predecessor deleted or fenced and the default flipped (the `None→0.0` default is gone, no\n  zero-deletion \"migration\"); every proof packet is run-emitted and recomputed by its\n  validator, not authored; and F4/F7 closure is measured on a representative corpus or\n  marked `surface_out_of_scope`, never a 2-record fixture.\n- Slice 0 is not credited as policy-design synthesis: no `DesignCandidate` promotion is\n  expected until the Phase-2 lowering/drafter/lex path is subordinated.\n- **Deep Workability Verification (Phase 7) passes by execution:** the coverage matrix\n  closes (GY-V1); a real loop run produces a measurement-rooted grounded/limited design\n  or a ceiling-gate-certified honest abstention (GY-V2); the generalization distribution\n  is recorded without forcing useful-design credit (GY-V3); all listed adversarial probes\n  fail closed (GY-V4); replay levels A/B/C hold and hashes are reproducible (GY-V5); the\n  full validator suite is green with no uncatalogued drift (GY-V6); the five health\n  signals are recorded with the honest domain-vs-search-ceiling interpretation (GY-V7).\n"
    },
